summary: The trapdoor (CWE-510) is the hidden, hostname-based privilege escalation in bad(): the code reads the client's reverse-DNS hostname via socket.getInetAddress().getHostName() and, if it equals the hardcoded "admin.google.com", serves the privileged "Welcome, admin!" response. Reverse-DNS hostnames are attacker-controllable (an attacker who controls PTR records for their IP can make it resolve to any name), so this constitutes a backdoor granting elevated access on a spoofable condition. The fix removes the hidden hostname-based branch entirely while preserving the legitimate feature: the server still accepts the connection and writes the standard welcome message to the connected client. No elevated/backdoor path remains, and ordinary connections continue to be served normally.
